summary: Junkichi Imanishi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1959–1965) and under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1965–1968). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1969–1998), the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1993–2007), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2017).

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the Australian National University (~1978–1980) and completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen (~1984–1990), later serving as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Otani University until around 1973 and held a post at Kansai University.

Junsho Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Étienne Lamotte, Juntaka Kato, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura. He held professorships at Nishogakusha University (1972) and Nagoya University (~1980–2003).

Junyi Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1925–1926) and under Thomé H. Fang and Shili Xiong. He held posts at National Central University (~1944–1949) and as a professor at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1953–1978).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section head (課長) at Otani University.
Juro Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1984–1991) and held a post at the University of Tsukuba.
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University.

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside (~2006–2008) and became Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania around 2008.

Justin R. Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2003–2010), held visiting scholar roles at Academia Sinica and Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and became a professor at Oberlin College around 2013.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~2007–2012) under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justus Olshausen was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer. He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1823–1848) and the University of Königsberg (1853).

János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1975–1980) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1986–1988).
Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May. He has held a post at the University of Lausanne in the Department of Oriental Languages and Cultures.

Józef Kowalewski was a linguist and scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan Imperial University, later holding posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1828–1860), Kazan Federal University (rector in 1855), and the University of Warsaw (~1862–1878).
József Budenz was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (~1855–1858). He held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from around 1872 to 1892.

Jörg Heimbel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tibet University and the University of Hamburg (PhD ~2008–2014) under David P. Jackson, Dorji Wangchuk, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later lecturing in Tibetan at the University of Hamburg in 2014.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (~2007).

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1999–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as an associate professor there from around 2005 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1994–1997) and studied under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2000–2007) and became a professor at the University of Marburg around 2007.
